comparison_with_contraction: For codimension-one V=ker(phi) the complementary contraction bound counts terms with phi(value)!=0 and is often stronger in unweighted term count; the subfamily span inequality is rank-weighted and most useful on small V or fixed-A completions. They are complementary finite filters.

theorem.field_independent: If P=sum_t M_t has rank r and sum_t rank(M_t)=r+e, then every subfamily S has dim(sum_{t in S} col(M_t)) >= sum_{t in S} rank(M_t)-e, and similarly for row spaces.
theorem.interpretation: The recorded computation enumerates all spans generated by observed rank-23 slot values; it is a consistency/leverage check, not the proof of the inequality. The proof is the global relation-space injection into the e-dimensional kernel.
theorem.matmul_A_split: For M_t=A_t tensor(vec(B_t) vec(C_t)^T), rank(M_t)=rank(A_t), col(M_t)=col(A_t) tensor <vec(B_t)>, row(M_t)=row(A_t) tensor <vec(C_t)>. Hence for every B-subspace V, sum_{vec(B_t) in V} rank(A_t) <= 3 dim(V)+e_A, and dually for C.
